request.system:
You explain a fitted credit-risk model to a credit risk manager who is not a data scientist. You receive the facts about one model and write a short explanation of what drives its predictions of default.

# The text

- Write 5 to 8 sentences in plain English, most important drivers first.
- Mention an interaction when it matters for the model's predictions.
- Say only what the facts support. Do not round a weak effect up to a strong one, and do not add knowledge about credit risk that the facts do not show.
- When the facts do not settle something, say so ("the data do not settle whether ...") or leave it out.

# The answer

Return one JSON object with one list, `sentences`, each with an `id` (1, 2, 3, ...) and its `text`.
messages:
These are the facts about the model.

Model: a gradient-boosted tree model of depth 2 (XGB2), fitted to predict whether a credit applicant defaults (5,000 applicants). Effects are on the log-odds scale: positive values raise the risk of default. Every band is a 95% band from 100 refits of the model on resampled data.

Features, in the order of their share of the model's importance:
- `PAY_0`: repayment status in September 2005, the latest month (-1 paid in full, 1 to 9 months of payment delay; -2 and 0 are not in the data dictionary, commonly read as no consumption and revolving credit used).
  Share of importance 28.7% (95% band 21.0% to 42.7%); rank 1 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): 0: -0.36; 1: +0.5; >= 2: +2 (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile +2.20, 95% band [+1.76, +2.43]).
- `LIMIT_BAL`: amount of the given credit in NT dollars, individual and family (supplementary) credit.
  Share of importance 17.5% (95% band 12.9% to 23.6%); rank 2 to 3 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): <= 219999: +0.16; >= 220000: -0.5 (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile -1.09, 95% band [-1.43, -0.44]).
- `PAY_AMT1`: amount paid in September 2005, the latest month, in NT dollars.
  Share of importance 10.6% (95% band 6.0% to 17.2%); rank 2 to 4 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): falls by 0.60 (95% band [-0.97, -0.22]) from x = 0 (5th percentile) to x = 17,000 (95th percentile); the shape in between is not resolved at this sample size.
- `BILL_AMT2`: amount of the bill statement in August 2005, the month before, in NT dollars.
  Share of importance 3.7% (95% band 0.0% to 5.9%); rank 4 to 9 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): no movement resolved at this sample size (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile +0.18, 95% band [-0.18, +0.34]).
- `BILL_AMT1`: amount of the bill statement in September 2005, the latest month, in NT dollars.
  Share of importance 2.8% (95% band 0.2% to 7.3%); rank 4 to 9 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): no movement resolved at this sample size (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile +0.18, 95% band [-0.10, +0.43]).
- `EDUCATION`: education (1 graduate school, 2 university, 3 high school, 4 others; 0, 5 and 6 are not in the data dictionary).
  Share of importance 2.5% (95% band 0.9% to 7.4%); rank 3 to 9 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): rises by 0.17 (95% band [+0.01, +0.36]) from x = 1 (5th percentile) to x = 3 (95th percentile); the shape in between is not resolved at this sample size.
- `AGE`: age in years.
  Share of importance 2.2% (95% band 0.0% to 5.5%); rank 4 to 9 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): no movement resolved at this sample size (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile -0.05, 95% band [-0.35, +0.29]).
- `PAY_AMT3`: amount paid in July 2005, two months before, in NT dollars.
  Share of importance 1.6% (95% band 0.0% to 4.4%); rank 4 to 9 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): no movement resolved at this sample size (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile -0.09, 95% band [-0.25, +0.10]).
- `PAY_AMT2`: amount paid in August 2005, the month before, in NT dollars.
  Share of importance 1.2% (95% band 0.0% to 5.4%); rank 4 to 9 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): no movement resolved at this sample size (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile +0.07, 95% band [-0.27, +0.27]).

Interactions: the model has 30 pairs. The larger ones:
- `PAY_0 & EDUCATION`: share of importance 10.9% (95% band 7.8% to 14.2%).
  Effect of `PAY_0` from -2 to 2: +1.62 (95% band +1.29 to +1.93) when `EDUCATION` = 1, +4.30 (95% band +2.99 to +4.92) when `EDUCATION` = 3.
  Effect of `EDUCATION` from 1 to 3: -0.31 (95% band -0.55 to +0.00) when `PAY_0` = -2, +2.37 (95% band +1.38 to +2.87) when `PAY_0` = 2.
- `AGE & BILL_AMT2`: share of importance 2.6% (95% band 0.0% to 1.8%).
  Effect of `AGE` from 23 to 53: +0.03 (95% band -0.32 to +0.33) when `BILL_AMT2` = 0, -0.48 (95% band -0.39 to +0.25) when `BILL_AMT2` = 196,000.
  Effect of `BILL_AMT2` from 0 to 196,000: +0.34 (95% band -0.18 to +0.36) when `AGE` = 23, -0.16 (95% band -0.20 to +0.28) when `AGE` = 53.
- `PAY_0 & LIMIT_BAL`: share of importance 1.4% (95% band 0.7% to 4.0%).
  Effect of `PAY_0` from -2 to 2: +2.20 (95% band +1.66 to +2.51) when `LIMIT_BAL` = 20,000, +1.90 (95% band +1.47 to +2.48) when `LIMIT_BAL` = 430,000.
  Effect of `LIMIT_BAL` from 20,000 to 430,000: -0.92 (95% band -1.19 to -0.41) when `PAY_0` = -2, -1.21 (95% band -1.48 to -0.38) when `PAY_0` = 2.
- `PAY_0 & PAY_AMT3`: share of importance 1.3% (95% band 0.0% to 1.8%).
  Effect of `PAY_0` from -2 to 2: +2.09 (95% band +1.76 to +2.42) when `PAY_AMT3` = 0, +2.27 (95% band +1.78 to +2.56) when `PAY_AMT3` = 18,100.
  Effect of `PAY_AMT3` from 0 to 18,100: -0.21 (95% band -0.37 to +0.10) when `PAY_0` = -2, -0.03 (95% band -0.25 to +0.25) when `PAY_0` = 2.
- `PAY_0 & PAY_AMT1`: share of importance 1.2% (95% band 0.7% to 3.5%).
  Effect of `PAY_0` from -2 to 2: +2.02 (95% band +1.58 to +2.15) when `PAY_AMT1` = 0, +2.35 (95% band +1.90 to +2.75) when `PAY_AMT1` = 17,000.
  Effect of `PAY_AMT1` from 0 to 17,000: -0.66 (95% band -1.07 to -0.25) when `PAY_0` = -2, -0.33 (95% band -0.51 to +0.07) when `PAY_0` = 2.
- `LIMIT_BAL & BILL_AMT1`: share of importance 1.1% (95% band 0.0% to 1.6%).
  Effect of `LIMIT_BAL` from 20,000 to 430,000: -0.91 (95% band -1.37 to -0.36) when `BILL_AMT1` = 0, -1.06 (95% band -1.50 to -0.43) when `BILL_AMT1` = 201,000.
  Effect of `BILL_AMT1` from 0 to 201,000: +0.16 (95% band -0.14 to +0.48) when `LIMIT_BAL` = 20,000, +0.01 (95% band -0.28 to +0.46) when `LIMIT_BAL` = 430,000.
- `LIMIT_BAL & BILL_AMT2`: share of importance 1.0% (95% band 0.0% to 1.6%).
  Effect of `LIMIT_BAL` from 20,000 to 430,000: -1.02 (95% band -1.35 to -0.43) when `BILL_AMT2` = 0, -1.60 (95% band -1.87 to -0.44) when `BILL_AMT2` = 196,000.
  Effect of `BILL_AMT2` from 0 to 196,000: +0.71 (95% band -0.06 to +0.69) when `LIMIT_BAL` = 20,000, +0.12 (95% band -0.24 to +0.25) when `LIMIT_BAL` = 430,000.
- `LIMIT_BAL & PAY_AMT1`: share of importance 1.0% (95% band 0.2% to 2.7%).
  Effect of `LIMIT_BAL` from 20,000 to 430,000: -1.08 (95% band -1.32 to -0.35) when `PAY_AMT1` = 0, -1.07 (95% band -1.55 to -0.52) when `PAY_AMT1` = 17,000.
  Effect of `PAY_AMT1` from 0 to 17,000: -0.62 (95% band -0.97 to -0.13) when `LIMIT_BAL` = 20,000, -0.61 (95% band -1.06 to -0.19) when `LIMIT_BAL` = 430,000.
- `LIMIT_BAL & PAY_AMT3`: share of importance 0.9% (95% band 0.0% to 2.1%).
  Effect of `LIMIT_BAL` from 20,000 to 430,000: -1.01 (95% band -1.37 to -0.43) when `PAY_AMT3` = 0, -1.14 (95% band -1.45 to -0.45) when `PAY_AMT3` = 18,100.
  Effect of `PAY_AMT3` from 0 to 18,100: -0.01 (95% band -0.29 to +0.23) when `LIMIT_BAL` = 20,000, -0.14 (95% band -0.37 to +0.12) when `LIMIT_BAL` = 430,000.
- `PAY_AMT1 & AGE`: share of importance 0.9% (95% band 0.0% to 2.3%).
  Effect of `PAY_AMT1` from 0 to 17,000: -0.50 (95% band -0.95 to -0.12) when `AGE` = 23, -0.65 (95% band -1.14 to -0.26) when `AGE` = 53.
  Effect of `AGE` from 23 to 53: +0.01 (95% band -0.28 to +0.42) when `PAY_AMT1` = 0, -0.14 (95% band -0.37 to +0.21) when `PAY_AMT1` = 17,000.
- `PAY_0 & BILL_AMT1`: share of importance 0.9% (95% band 0.0% to 2.2%).
  Effect of `PAY_0` from -2 to 2: +1.80 (95% band +1.36 to +2.26) when `BILL_AMT1` = 0, +2.12 (95% band +1.58 to +2.45) when `BILL_AMT1` = 201,000.
  Effect of `BILL_AMT1` from 0 to 201,000: +0.27 (95% band -0.07 to +0.67) when `PAY_0` = -2, +0.58 (95% band -0.18 to +0.99) when `PAY_0` = 2.
- `LIMIT_BAL & PAY_AMT2`: share of importance 0.8% (95% band 0.0% to 2.3%).
  Effect of `LIMIT_BAL` from 20,000 to 430,000: -1.12 (95% band -1.39 to -0.43) when `PAY_AMT2` = 0, -1.16 (95% band -1.49 to -0.44) when `PAY_AMT2` = 17,900.
  Effect of `PAY_AMT2` from 0 to 17,900: +0.14 (95% band -0.32 to +0.42) when `LIMIT_BAL` = 20,000, +0.11 (95% band -0.31 to +0.35) when `LIMIT_BAL` = 430,000.
- `PAY_AMT1 & BILL_AMT2`: share of importance 0.8% (95% band 0.0% to 1.7%).
  Effect of `PAY_AMT1` from 0 to 17,000: -0.62 (95% band -1.10 to -0.13) when `BILL_AMT2` = 0, -0.71 (95% band -1.14 to -0.22) when `BILL_AMT2` = 196,000.
  Effect of `BILL_AMT2` from 0 to 196,000: +0.27 (95% band -0.18 to +0.46) when `PAY_AMT1` = 0, +0.18 (95% band -0.23 to +0.31) when `PAY_AMT1` = 17,000.
- `BILL_AMT1 & AGE`: share of importance 0.7% (95% band 0.0% to 3.1%).
  Effect of `BILL_AMT1` from 0 to 201,000: +0.20 (95% band -0.11 to +0.68) when `AGE` = 23, +0.10 (95% band -0.28 to +0.36) when `AGE` = 53.
  Effect of `AGE` from 23 to 53: +0.00 (95% band -0.26 to +0.37) when `BILL_AMT1` = 0, -0.10 (95% band -0.51 to +0.20) when `BILL_AMT1` = 201,000.
- `PAY_AMT2 & AGE`: share of importance 0.5% (95% band 0.0% to 1.1%).
  Effect of `PAY_AMT2` from 0 to 17,900: +0.10 (95% band -0.43 to +0.30) when `AGE` = 23, +0.06 (95% band -0.26 to +0.26) when `AGE` = 53.
  Effect of `AGE` from 23 to 53: -0.02 (95% band -0.35 to +0.24) when `PAY_AMT2` = 0, -0.06 (95% band -0.35 to +0.39) when `PAY_AMT2` = 17,900.
- 15 further pairs with a share below 0.5% each, together 3.2%.

Write the explanation.

content.text: {"sentences":[{"id":1,"text":"The model's predictions of default are driven mainly by the applicant's most recent repayment status (PAY_0), which accounts for about 29% of the model's importance; applicants who were already two or more months behind (2 or higher) carry a much higher predicted risk than those who paid in full."},{"id":2,"text":"Credit limit (LIMIT_BAL) is the second most important factor, at about 18%: applicants with a limit of 220,000 NT dollars or more are predicted to be lower risk than those below that level."},{"id":3,"text":"The amount paid in the latest month (PAY_AMT1) matters moderately, at about 11%: predicted risk falls as this payment rises from 0 to around 17,000 NT dollars, although the shape of the curve in between is not resolved by the data."},{"id":4,"text":"The effect of repayment status is considerably stronger for applicants with higher education levels: moving PAY_0 from -2 to 2 adds about 4.3 log-odds for education level 3 but only about 1.6 for education level 1, so the two factors should be read together."},{"id":5,"text":"Credit limit and repayment status also interact, but more weakly: the protective effect of a higher limit is somewhat smaller for applicants who are already behind on payments."},{"id":6,"text":"Bill amounts, age, and the earlier payment amounts (PAY_AMT2, PAY_AMT3) each contribute little on their own, and the data do not show a clear effect of their values on predicted default."},{"id":7,"text":"The effect of education on its own is modest, and the interval around it is wide enough that the direction of its effect is not firmly established by the data."}]}
